name: Palace
label: Drag City
lede: A teenage movie actor from Louisville, a rotating cast of Slint members and brothers, a new band name on almost every record, and a songbook Johnny Cash ended up singing.

eras.title: A boy preacher with a camera
eras.text: Before Palace, Will Oldham was a Louisville kid who'd acted for John Sayles and hung around the city's punk scene, close enough to Slint to shoot their most famous photo. By 1992 he was playing open mics under joke names and cutting his first single for a new Chicago label, Drag City.

years.h: Will Oldham plays a teen preacher in John Sayles' Matewan
years.p: At 17, Louisville's Will Oldham is cast as Danny Radnor, a boy preacher, in Matewan, John Sayles' film about the 1920 West Virginia coal war.
years.xp: Acting came first. Oldham kept taking film roles for decades, from Sayles' Thousand Pieces of Gold to Kelly Reichardt's Old Joy.

years.h: Will Oldham shoots the Spiderland cover: Slint in a quarry
years.p: Will Oldham takes the photo of [[Slint|2869c510-2679-4a3f-bf15-e5e8b49f2f28]] treading water in a Kentucky quarry that becomes the cover of Spiderland. Three of the heads in the water will soon play on Palace records.
years.xp: Slint's [[Britt Walford|7fde6efa-750a-49c1-abee-7767230407ff]], [[Brian McMahan|bebfec95-35a3-4cc8-b85e-8b178d09526d]] and [[David Pajo|85188c46-d3ed-4517-ba78-5d06ec764f1c]] all turn up on early Palace sessions. The Louisville circle was small: the same few people kept trading instruments.

years.h: Open mics as Grant's Tomb and Birdie Num Nums
years.p: Before Palace has a name, Will Oldham and friends play open mics in Bloomington, Indiana and Louisville as Grant's Tomb and Birdie Num Nums, plus a Derby party as Wing It.

years.h: Ohio River Boat Song: the first Palace Brothers 7-inch
years.p: Drag City issues Ohio River Boat Song backed with Drinking Woman, the first Palace Brothers single, recorded for the new Chicago label.

eras.title: Palace Brothers, whoever's in the room
eras.text: The first Palace records were old-time country played by Louisville post-rock musicians who barely knew the idiom, and that was the point. Oldham recorded with whoever was around, from Slint members in a shared house to his brothers in their parents' place, and toured Europe before most of America had heard him.

years.h: [[Royal Trux|87e27246-8c40-407f-bfb3-5dc416557eeb]] talk Drag City into signing Will Oldham
years.p: According to Stereogum, [[Neil Hagerty|dabacddd-26f0-45b9-b6eb-17fa31af7329]] and [[Jennifer Herrema|4e505aec-707e-49b3-a2f3-b8c6513549e2]] of Royal Trux pushed Drag City to sign Will Oldham, then produced the Palace Brothers single Come In under the name Adam and Eve.

years.h: First official show: opening the Big Star reunion
years.p: Palace Brothers' first listed date is at the University of Missouri in Columbia, opening for [[Big Star|21d177ba-3d51-461e-9b3f-ad9a80b419dc]], the night Alex Chilton's band reunited.

years.h: There Is No-One What Will Take Care of You: country from Slint
years.p: Palace Brothers' first album is made with Louisville players including Slint's [[Britt Walford|7fde6efa-750a-49c1-abee-7767230407ff]] and [[Brian McMahan|bebfec95-35a3-4cc8-b85e-8b178d09526d]], [[Todd Brashear|9fecf563-bce8-4960-89e9-7075bbffe84f]] on lap steel and Grant Barger on organ. The one cover is Washington Phillips' I Had a Good Mother and Father.
years.xp:
The musicians swapped guitar, bass and drums between songs, which is why the record wobbles like a front-porch session. The Toronto Star called it quietly beautiful and slightly askew.

Mojo later put it in The Mojo Collection: The Greatest Albums of All Time (2001).
play: There Is No-One What Will Take Care of You
I Had a Good Mother and Father

years.h: Drag City Invitational at Lounge Ax, Chicago
years.p: Palace plays Drag City's three-night showcase at Chicago's Lounge Ax, on bills with [[Silver Jews|1bc2d696-c0e2-480d-87ed-17b2a82d7983]], [[Smog|89af9575-4d72-4345-8eba-e9de3d36ac34]] and [[Pavement|36bfa85f-737b-41db-a8fc-b8825850ffc3]].

years.h: First European tour, Ireland to Germany
years.p: Palace Brothers tour Ireland, the UK, the Netherlands and Germany with Todd Brashear, Britt Walford and Brian McMahan in the band.

years.h: Horses 7-inch, cut in Bob Nastanovich's house
years.p: The third Palace single is recorded in a house Will Oldham shared with [[Bob Nastanovich|4bcaf5b5-89a5-4712-8a11-6d60dd0904f5]] and Britt Walford. Horses is a Sally Timms and Jon Langford song Oldham had sung for years; [[David Pajo|85188c46-d3ed-4517-ba78-5d06ec764f1c]] overdubs guitar.
years.xp: Brian McMahan played drums, Britt Walford bass and Todd Brashear lap steel. The B-side, Stable Will, came from sessions in an abandoned Louisville building with the Pale Horse Riders, and was mostly written by Bryan Rich under the name Roy Black.

years.h: Palace on the 1994 Lollapalooza tour
years.p: Per the fan database Royal Stable, Palace spends mid-July to early August 1994 on the Lollapalooza tour across North America.

years.h: Days in the Wake: Will Oldham alone with a cassette deck
years.p: Will Oldham makes the second Palace Brothers album almost solo on a Marantz cassette recorder bought from Bryan Rich, mostly at his parents' house in Louisville. It ships with no title at all.
years.xp:
More sessions happened at brother [[Ned Oldham|57b40135-dad3-4514-9e28-fc446cf20585]]'s house in Birmingham, Alabama; Ned plays bass and Paul Oldham percussion on one track. The name Days in the Wake came later.

AllMusic's Mark Deming called it the simplest record in the Palace canon, and among the best.
play: You Will Miss Me When I Burn

years.h: Hope EP: Palace Songs, on purpose grateful
years.p: Billed as Palace Songs, Hope was meant as a turn toward gratitude after Days in the Wake. Cut at Chicago's Acme with [[Liam Hayes|bb2c8e53-ff20-429e-b095-50c39ee0c393]] on keys, plus London sessions with [[Sean O'Hagan|62b38d85-b2b9-4c59-8b86-9336c6e58491]]; it includes a Leonard Cohen cover.

years.h: The Palace Revue and Motor Show
years.p: A Midwest tour billed as the Palace Revue and Motor Show ends in St. Louis with a run of Elvis covers.

eras.title: A new name for every band
eras.text: Palace Brothers became Palace Songs, then Palace Music, then just Will Oldham, because the line-up kept changing and Oldham thought the name should too. These are the records, cut with Steve Albini, that made the reputation.

years.big: Palace Brothers. Palace Songs. Palace Music. Palace.
q: the same group of people playing on it
years.h: Why Palace kept changing its name
years.p: Will Oldham said a band name promises the same players on the next record. Palace never had the same players, so the name changed.
years.xp: Oldham explained that when a group keeps its name, listeners expect the next record to have the same people on it. Since Palace was whoever turned up, he rotated the name instead. By 1997 he was releasing under his own name, and a year later as Bonnie "Prince" Billy.

years.h: Viva Last Blues: Palace Music goes full band with Steve Albini
years.p: Recorded in Alabama with [[Steve Albini|a4d486bd-6020-4a36-9c7d-bf5ce174bcd1]], Viva Last Blues is the loud Palace record: Bryan Rich on lead guitar, [[Ned Oldham|57b40135-dad3-4514-9e28-fc446cf20585]] on bass, [[Liam Hayes|bb2c8e53-ff20-429e-b095-50c39ee0c393]] on keys and [[Sebadoh|d98c8149-0c01-4151-93e1-48fdc3d5027f]]'s [[Jason Loewenstein|d06bfcfa-7be5-40ca-82be-4c7d3bdb44c3]] on drums.
years.xp:
NME and Spin both gave it 8/10. Pitchfork later ranked it No. 60 on its list of the top 100 albums of the 1990s.

John Green gave New Partner four stars on The Anthropocene Reviewed in 2019.

years.h: Arise Therefore: Albini, David Grubbs and a drum machine
years.p: Palace Music's Arise Therefore is cut by Steve Albini at Pachyderm Studio in Cannon Falls, Minnesota, with [[David Grubbs|f72e65e9-3ee7-4dce-9c53-5dc6221f6cd3]] on piano and organ and a Mayatone drum machine credited as a member, "Maya Tone".
years.xp: Alternative Press gave it five out of five. Mojo called it a phantom creation beyond the comprehension of even its creator.

years.h: Joya: the first record as plain Will Oldham
years.p: Palace is retired as a name. Joya comes out under Will Oldham's own name.

years.h: Lost Blues and Other Songs gathers the Palace singles
years.p: Drag City collects the scattered Palace 7-inches, from Ohio River Boat Song on, onto one album.

eras.title: Bonnie "Prince" Billy and the Man in Black
eras.text: From 1998 Oldham worked as Bonnie "Prince" Billy, and the Palace songs found singers far bigger than him. He kept acting too, from Kelly Reichardt films to a Kanye West video.

years.h: Will Oldham becomes Bonnie "Prince" Billy
years.p: The new name mixes Bonnie Prince Charlie, Nat King Cole and Billy the Kid (William Bonney).

years.h: I See a Darkness, the first Bonnie "Prince" Billy album
years.p: Will Oldham's first record as Bonnie "Prince" Billy is the one critics still reach for first.

years.h: [[Johnny Cash|d43d12a1-2dc9-4257-a2fd-0a3bb1081b86]] sings I See a Darkness
years.p: Johnny Cash records Will Oldham's I See a Darkness for American III: Solitary Man, with Oldham singing backup.

years.h: Will Oldham sings on [[Silver Jews|1bc2d696-c0e2-480d-87ed-17b2a82d7983]]' Tanglewood Numbers
years.p: Will Oldham joins [[David Berman|bbed0b05-cf87-45e6-aee8-259b34077969]], [[Stephen Malkmus|eaefd603-84c1-4db4-a72b-0cb718a0cc07]] and [[Bob Nastanovich|4bcaf5b5-89a5-4712-8a11-6d60dd0904f5]] on the 2005 Silver Jews album, twelve years after their Drag City Invitational bill.

years.h: Will Oldham stars in Kelly Reichardt's Old Joy
years.p: Will Oldham plays Kurt, the drifter friend on a camping trip, in Old Joy.

years.h: Will Oldham in Kanye West's Can't Tell Me Nothing video
years.p: Kanye West's alternate video for Can't Tell Me Nothing is Will Oldham and Zach Galifianakis lip-syncing on a farm.

years.cap: Elsa and Will Oldham. Photo: Christian Hansen
years.h: Will Oldham marries Elsa Hansen
years.p: Will Oldham marries textile artist Elsa Hansen; their child is born in 2018.
